en: The *Bhadracaryāpraṇidhāna* (1) As many lions among men as there are in the worlds of the ten directions throughout all three times, I pay homage to them all without exception, with body, speech, and mind full of faith.

(2) With bodies as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-fields, I prostrate before all the Victors with a mind directed toward all the Victors, by the power of the vow of the Excellent Conduct (*Bhadracaryā*). (3) Upon the tip of a single atom are Buddhas as numerous as atoms, with the sons of the Buddhas seated in their midst; in this way, I resolve with total conviction that the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is filled with Victors.

(2) IV. And within those [oceans of worlds], praising the virtues of all the Victors with oceans of inexhaustible qualities through the sounds of oceans of all vocal qualities, I offer praise to all those Sugatas.

V. With the finest flowers and the finest garlands, with musical instruments, ointments, and the finest parasols, (3) with the finest lamps and the finest incense, I perform worship for those Victors.
VI. With the finest garments, the finest perfumes, and handfuls of powdered incense as vast as Mount Meru, and with all the most excellent and sublime arrays, I perform worship to those Victors.
VII. Whatever unsurpassed and magnificent worship there is, I resolve upon it for all the Victors; through the power of my resolve for auspicious conduct, I pay homage to and worship all the Victors.
VIII. And whatever sin I may have committed under the influence of passion, hatred, or delusion—whether by body, speech, or mind—I confess it all.

IX. And whatever merit there is in the ten directions belonging to those in training and those beyond training, to the Pratyekabuddhas, to the sons of the Buddhas, and to all the Victors—that I rejoice in all of it. X. And those lamps of the world in the ten directions who have awakened to enlightenment and attained non-attachment—to all those Protectors I entreat, that they turn the unsurpassed wheel. XI. And those who desire to manifest final nirvana, to them I make my request with palms joined: may they remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a field, for the benefit and happiness of the entire world.
(6) XII. Whatever merit I have accumulated through prostration, worship, and confession; through rejoicing, entreaty, and supplication—I dedicate it all toward awakening.

(7) XIII. May the Buddhas of the past be honored; may those who currently dwell in the worlds of the ten directions, and those yet to come, quickly fulfill their aspirations and awaken to supreme enlightenment.
XIV. May all the realms in the ten directions become vast and utterly pure; may they be filled with Victors seated beneath the sovereign trees of awakening, and with the sons of the Buddhas.

(8) XV May all sentient beings whatsoever in the ten directions always be happy and free from illness; may the righteous purpose of the entire world be fulfilled, and may their hopes be successfully realized. XVI And while practicing the conduct of awakening, may I remember my births in all states of existence; in every life, through death and rebirth, may I always go forth into the religious life. (9) XVII Training myself in the teachings of all the Victors and fulfilling the Excellent Conduct, may I always practice the stainless and pure conduct of ethical discipline, unbroken and without flaw.

XVIII. Through the languages of gods, the languages of nāgas, the languages of yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and humans—whatever languages there are in the world—I shall teach the Dharma in all those languages.
XIX. May I be skillful and devoted to the perfections, and may my mind for awakening never be deluded; furthermore, may all evil obstructions be completely exhausted without remainder. XX.
From karma, from afflictions, and from the path of Māra, may I wander liberated among the worldly realms, unstained like a lotus by water, unattached like the sun and moon in the sky.

(11) XXI. May I pacify all the sufferings of the miserable realms and establish the entire world; may I practice for the benefit of the whole world throughout as many fields and directions as there are. XXII. Following the conduct of sentient beings, fulfilling the conduct of awakening, and manifesting the auspicious conduct, may I practice through all future eons. (12) XXIII. And may I always meet with those who share my conduct, whether in body, speech, or intention; may I practice the vow of a single conduct.

XXIV. May I always meet with those friends who desire my welfare and who show me the way of auspicious conduct; may I never at any time cause them to be displeased. XXV. Upholding the true Dharma of the Victors, illuminating the practice of enlightenment, and purifying the way of auspicious conduct, may I practice throughout all future eons.
XXVI. May I always behold the Victors face-to-face, surrounded by their sons, the Buddhas; and toward them, may I perform sublime worship, untiring throughout all future eons.

(14) XXVII. And while wandering through all states of existence, may he attain inexhaustibility in merit and wisdom; through wisdom, skillful means, meditative concentrations, and liberations, may he become an inexhaustible treasury of all virtues.

XXVIII. On the tip of a single atom, may he see Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms, and within those fields, may he behold inconceivable Buddhas seated in their midst, while he himself practices the conduct of enlightenment.

(15) XXIX. Thus, throughout all directions without exception, even in the paths of a single hair, may he enter oceans of Buddhas, oceans of fields, and oceans of aeons of practice, equal in measure to the three times.

(XXX) With the ocean-like sounds of the single vocal organ, may I always enter into the Buddha’s eloquence—the purity of the vocal organs of all Victors and the voices that accord with the inclinations of the entire world. (16) (XXXI) And within those inexhaustible sounds and tones, may I, by the power of my intelligence, enter into the turning of the wheel of the Dharma of all the Victors who have gone throughout the three times. (XXXII) In a single instant, may I enter into all future eons; and even those eons whose measure is equal to the three times, may I practice having entered into them as millions of instants.

(17) XXXIII. And those lions among men who have appeared throughout the three times, may I behold them all in a single instant; and may I always enter their sphere of activity by means of the power of liberation that consists in the nature of illusion.

XXXIV. And whatever arrays of buddha-fields exist throughout the three times, may I manifest them upon the tip of a single atom; thus, without exception, may I enter into the arrays of the fields of all the Victors in every direction. (18) XXXV. And those lamps of the world who are yet to come—may I approach all those Protectors as they awaken, turn the wheel of Dharma, and display their final peace in parinirvāṇa.

XXXVI. By the power of supernatural transformations with universal speed, by the power of the vehicle with universal gates, by the power of conduct with universal virtues, and by the power of loving-kindness reaching everywhere;

(19) XXXVII. By the power of merit that is universally auspicious, by the power of knowledge that reaches the unattached, and by the power of wisdom, skillful means, and meditative concentration, he fully accumulates the power of enlightenment.
XXXVIII. Purifying the power of karma, crushing the power of the afflictions, and rendering the power of Māra powerless, he fulfills all the powers of the noble conduct.
(20) XXXIX Purifying oceans of fields, liberating oceans of sentient beings, discerning oceans of Dharma, and plunging into oceans of gnosis;
XL purifying oceans of conduct, fulfilling oceans of vows, and honoring oceans of Buddhas, may I practice through oceans of eons without weariness.

(21) XLI Whatever specific qualities of the awakening-conduct and vows of the Victors who have gone throughout the three times—may I fulfill them all without exception, and awaken to enlightenment through the *Bhadracarī*.
XLII. To that eldest son of all the Victors, whose name is Samantabhadra—to that wise one, for the sake of his shared conduct, I dedicate all this merit.

XLIII. May there be purity of body, speech, and mind; may there be purity of conduct and purity of the field. Just as is the name of the wise Bhadra, may I become equal to him in that regard. XLIV. Through the universally auspicious conduct of Bhadra, may I practice the vow of Mañjuśrī; throughout all future eons, without weariness, may I fulfill every single one of those deeds without exception.

(23) XLV. There would be no measure to my conduct, nor would there be any measure to my virtues; established in immeasurable conduct, I know all their miraculous transformations. XLVI. As far as the limit of space may extend, and as far as the limit of sentient beings without exception, and as far as the limit of karma and afflictions—so far extends my vow. (24) XLVII. And those who, in the infinite fields of the ten directions, were to give to the Victors lands adorned with jewels, along with divine and human excellences of happiness, for eons equal to the dust-motes of those fields;
XLVIII. And whoever, having heard this king of dedications, should once produce resolute faith while aspiring for supreme enlightenment—this merit shall become foremost and most distinguished.
XLIX. By him the states of woe are avoided; by him evil friends are avoided; he quickly beholds that Amitābha, whose vow is this "Noble Conduct" (*Bhadracaryā*).
L. Well-gained is their gain, well-lived is their life; welcome to them is this human birth! For such as they are Samantabhadra, and they too shall before long become just like him.

(26) L I. Whoever, under the power of ignorance, has committed the five evil deeds of immediate retribution, shall quickly exhaust them without remainder by reciting this *Bhadracaryā*. LII. Endowed with wisdom, physical form, marks, complexion, and noble lineage, he becomes invincible to the hosts of heretics and Māras, and is honored throughout the three worlds.

LIII. He quickly goes to the king of Bodhi trees; having gone there, he sits for the benefit of sentient beings, awakens to enlightenment, turns the wheel [of Dharma], and subdues all Māra together with his entire army.

(27) LVI. Whoever shall uphold, recite, or teach this vow of the conduct of Samantabhadra—the Buddha knows the ripening of the fruit therein, which is distinguished by supreme enlightenment; do not give rise to doubt! LVII. With all that merit, I dedicate it all toward the supreme and noble conduct of Samantabhadra, according to that foremost dedication praised by all the Victors who have gone throughout the three times.
(28) LVIII. And when I am performing my final act of passing away, having removed all obscurations, may I behold Amitābha face to face and go to that realm of Sukhāvatī.

(29) LVIII. Having gone there, may all these vows of mine be fulfilled in their entirety; and having completed them without exception, may I bring about the welfare of beings as far as they exist in the world.

LIX. There, born within that beautiful and delightful assembly of the Jina upon a most excellent and radiant lotus, may I receive a prophecy of enlightenment directly from the Jina Amitābha. LX. Having received that prophecy, may I, by the power of my wisdom, perform manifold deeds for the benefit of sentient beings throughout the ten directions through many hundreds of millions of emanations.
(30) LXII. By the infinite, most excellent merit obtained through dedicating the *Bhadracaryā*, may the world, submerged in a flood of calamities, go to the supreme city of Amitābha.

LXI. Whatever slight virtue I have accumulated by reciting the *Bhadracaryāpraṇidhāna*, may it all be perfected in a single instant, and by that, may the auspicious aspiration of the world be fulfilled. (31)
